pr_body:
Fixes: #16874

This is a significant simplication of our startup code model for Blazor
wasm with the goal of removing concepts that don't make much sense here.
Previously in this area we've tried to be consistent with ASP.NET Core
on the server, but it's not helping up much in WASM.

We're still leveraging some of the lessons from server-size ASP.NET
(hello CreateDefaultBuilder) but consistency is no longer a goal.

This change actually makes a bunch of scenarios better (rather than
removing features) - it's now possible to access services from the
application's DI scope and initialize them before the UI is shown
`RunAsync`.

This change also adds configuration in a central way. There's nothing in
this change that populates configuration in an automatic way, that will
come next.

comments: We should make sure https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/issues/13694 is considered for `Startup API` review part.
Another reason why it would be good to have access to JSRuntime inside ConfigureServices [can be found here.](https://github.com/serilog/serilog-sinks-browserconsole/issues/8)

I like it!

It's simple and straightforward.

One question that arises, and its a minor thing. How do you expect this to interact with pre-rendering?

Do you expect people to duplicate service registrations?
Will we suggest people to move service registrations into a separate method?

Another interesting thing to think about, is would we flow some data like the environment from the server?
Does it make sense for us to do that?

> Do you expect people to duplicate service registrations?
> Will we suggest people to move service registrations into a separate method?

These are super good questions. I really do expect (for instance) that something like that would be needed. If your services talk to data you're going to need different implementations at the least.

I have a question : would it be a good idea to expose the renderer instance ? It could be nice for libraries that which to extend it (for instance I wanted to build MiniProfiler.Blazor but I couldn't find any good global hook, exposing WebRenderer would help I think). Maybe this is not related to this issue ...

Closing as done. 

@RemiBou can you file a separate issue for that discussion? I think we'd want to know more about this. We don't consider the renderer APIs to be stable right now, so we're not likely to put it in everyone's face.

BTW the decision we made for this in general (see DI) is that we block if someone calls `Dispose()`.
